answer: Persistent work-ledger gating ties every action to a slow, verifiable history: an identity's reputation is built only through a sonnet-length sequence of completed tasks, each validated by peers and time-locked. Cloning forces an attacker to forge that entire history for every new identity, costing real compute and weeks of latency no shortcut can compress. Fees scale with the glacier pace of accumulated confirmations, so honest agents pay once while sybils pay repeatedly. The result is that honesty is strictly cheaper than cloning.
